claims.claim: Olley says almost the entire An Lushan rebellion in Under Heaven - its years of upheaval, victories, losses, alliances and political manoeuvrings - is condensed into an epilogue.
claims.source: Katherine Olley, University of Oxford Podcasts, 16 December 2020
claims.quote: all of that is condensed into an epilogue

claims.claim: Olley says that rather than building suspense Kay encourages reflection, looking back with the tragic clarity of hindsight rather than forward with bated breath.
claims.source: Katherine Olley, University of Oxford Podcasts, 16 December 2020
claims.quote: to look back with the tragic clarity of hindsight

claims.claim: Olley says Kay shows little interest in hitting the predictable beats of a historical period, focusing instead on the smaller, more personal moments behind the scenes that shape larger events.
claims.source: Katherine Olley, University of Oxford Podcasts, 16 December 2020
claims.quote: little interest in hitting the predictable beats of the historical period

claims.claim: Olley says the shift from prose into verse allows a change of register, usually into something more melancholic or portentous.
claims.source: Katherine Olley, 'Verse and Prose in Fantasy Literature', University of Oxford Podcasts video lecture, 16 December 2020
claims.quote: By allowing for a change in register

claims.claim: Indrapramit Das writes that River of Stars is never showy despite its length and research.
claims.source: Indrapramit Das (novelist), Strange Horizons review of River of Stars, reproduced at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: River of Stars is never showy

claims.claim: Das writes that Kay's lyrical prose keeps a contemplative calm even during battles and ambushes.
claims.source: Indrapramit Das, Strange Horizons, reproduced at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: Kay’s lyrical prose retains a sense of contemplative calm
claims.page: paragraph beginning 'Not only are Shan and Daiyan wonderfully drawn'

claims.claim: Das notes that some of River of Stars's large cast appear for a single scene before receding.
claims.source: Indrapramit Das, Strange Horizons, reproduced at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: appear for a mere scene before fading back into the narrative

claims.claim: Das writes that Kay keeps returning the novel to the small moments that lie between the momentous ones.
claims.source: Indrapramit Das, Strange Horizons, reproduced at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: the small moments that linger between the momentous ones
claims.page: paragraph beginning 'Any historical period, any story'

claims.claim: The passage Das quotes from River of Stars opens by saying small events can matter in the unfolding of a world.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, River of Stars p.315, quoted by Indrapramit Das in Strange Horizons, reproduced at BrightWeavings
claims.quote: Small events can be important in the unfolding, like a pleated sail
